title: feat: add experimental plugin UI customization

commit.messageHeadline: feat: let plugins customize the Control UI
fix: harden feature plugin lifecycle and artifact activation
fix(plugins): complete native UI integration
fix(plugins): preserve hook ownership and composer styling
chore(workboard): refresh generated browser assets
test(android): hold reconciliation replies until delivery checks
refactor(plugins): simplify feature UI ownership
test(ui): return session snapshots from worker stop fixtures
fix(ui): hydrate session rosters from selected agents
perf(ui): defer plugin initialization and customization
refactor(ui): separate native asset loading from host services
test(plugins): align UI integration with current main
chore(workboard): refresh browser revision after rebase
chore(ui): refresh generated assets after main sync
fix(plugins): preserve native UI lifetimes after main sync
chore(ui): refresh boot manifest after main rebase
chore(ui): refresh feature integration after main update
test(ui): verify native plugin asset admission
test(ui): await service worker activation in phone proof
refactor(plugins): remove redundant UI plumbing
feat(plugins): gate custom UI behind an experimental lab
fix(plugins): align Labs helper types with callers
style(ui): format retained plugin panel definitions
test(ui): preserve minimized dashboard in native plugin flow
fix: preserve plugin UI edits and refresh ordering
test: align plugin UI proof with current panel layout
test: repair plugin UI validation and generated checkout helper
test: bind session search fixtures to their selection owner
fix: preserve session search ownership and execution denial proof
test: use a real page element for plugin sidebar fixtures
fix: respect native plugin UI deployment boundaries
test: share UI fixture isolation across runners
refactor: share the native plugin asset root
test: check failure trailers on their owning stream

Host and lifecycle enforcement: The host uses the existing Gateway client while activation ownership and retained contribution handles are retired on connection changes.
Asset authorization boundary: Gateway asset serving validates plugin revision and path, then requires a matching scoped grant or read authorization. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | Needs attention | Record acceptance for full operator authority: The public host lets enabled installed native UI issue Gateway requests under the operator's scopes; this is documented and default-off, but the intentional trust-boundary expansion requires SDK and security-owner approval before merge. | ## How this fits together Plugin manifests contribute UI assets and declarations through the Gateway, which authenticates and advertises them to Control UI. The Control UI runtime loads each admitted plugin with a lifecycle-bound host that can issue Gateway requests under the signed-in operator’s authority. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Installed plugin manifest] --> B[Gateway asset catalog] B --> C[Scoped asset authentication] C --> D[Control UI runtime] D --> E[Lifecycle-bound plugin host] E --> F[Plugin pages and actions] F --> G[Gateway requests with operator scopes] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Do SDK and security owners accept the default-off experimental design in which an enabled installed native Control UI plugin receives the signed-in operator's full Gateway authority? | **Accept the documented trusted-native model:** Record SDK and security-owner acceptance, then retain the Labs gate and complete exact-head validation. | Why: This is a new public SDK and authority boundary; code-level guards and documentation cannot determine whether the product's intended trust model is acceptable. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve security concern: Record acceptance for full operator authority** - The public host lets enabled installed native UI issue Gateway requests under the operator's scopes; this is documented and default-off, but the intentional trust-boundary expansion requires SDK and security-owner approval before merge. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - When enabled, installed native plugin code receives the signed-in operator's full Gateway authority, including administrative scopes; this deliberate trust expansion needs recorded SDK and security-owner acceptance. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The new default-off configuration and public SDK surface are upgrade-sensitive, while the supplied check list is truncated and does not independently establish exact-head completion. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Obtain recorded SDK and security-owner acceptance of the native installed-plugin authority model, then verify required checks on the exact head before merge. - [ ] **Resolve maintainer decision** - Resolve the maintainer decision shown above before merge. - [ ] **Review config compatibility** - Confirm compatibility and upgrade impact for the changed config or default surface before merge. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ## Findings - [medium] Record acceptance for full operator authority — `src/plugin-sdk/control-ui.ts:207`

Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Record acceptance and validate exact head (recommended)** Obtain SDK and security-owner acceptance of the full-authority model, then confirm all required checks on the exact PR head. 2. **Pause if authority sharing is unacceptable** Do not merge the public native-plugin API if owners require installed UI to be capability-scoped. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land only after SDK and security owners explicitly accept the documented default-off full-authority model and exact-head validation is confirmed, while retaining lifecycle-bound hosts, scoped asset authorization, and sandboxed alternatives. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Not applicable: this PR adds a new experimental capability rather than repairing a reported existing-behavior bug; its supplied browser and Gateway proof concerns feature behavior. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Unclear pending owner acceptance: the default-off, documented trusted-native model is coherent for full Control UI replacements, while sandboxed widgets and MCP Apps remain the safer path for isolated content. ([`ui/src/plugins/control-ui-host.ts:105`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33/ui/src/plugins/control-ui-host.ts#L105), [f1186148d930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33)) - **Asset authorization boundary:** Gateway asset serving validates plugin revision and path, then requires a matching scoped grant or read authorization. ([`src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.ts:354`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33/src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.ts#L354), [f1186148d930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33)) - **Boundary coverage:** Tests cover wrong plugin or generation grants, bearer-read access, and rejected source-map, hidden, and escape paths; runtime tests cover origin, secure-context, grant, and base-path admission. ([`src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts:432`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33/src/gateway/control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts#L432), [f1186148d930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33)) - **Documented trust model:** Documentation describes native UI as trusted same-origin code with full authority, default-off experimental enablement, HTTPS/loopback requirements, and sandboxed widgets or MCP Apps as the isolated alternative. Public docs: [`docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/feature-plugins). ([`docs/plugins/feature-plugins.md:19`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/plugins/feature-plugins), [f1186148d930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33)) - **Public SDK surface:** The package exports three Control UI Plugin SDK entrypoints, making this a public compatibility and trust boundary rather than an internal Workboard-only refactor. ([`package.json:1484`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33/package.json#L1484), [f1186148d930](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f1186148d9302ff7054dd2258982e730ceaf2b33)) Likely related people: - **steipete:** Suggested for follow-up; no historical authorship or introduction is verified. Shiny media proof means a screenshot, video, or linked artifact directly shows the changed behavior. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation. ### History
